Description: Options when implementing natural gas networks
Limits on imports compared to historical year
Minimum import requirememnt compared to historical year.
Maximum allowable imports compared to historical year.
Limits on exports compared to historical year
Minimum export requirememnt compared to historical year.
Maximum allowable exports compared to historical year.
Apply cyclic storage constraints on linepack and underground storage
Leakage rate from pipelines. These leaks do NOT account towards emissions, just enforces gas production to replinish losses with cyclic constraints.
Multiplier on the marginal cost of importing/exporting natural gas.
Multiplier on the existing pipeline capacity. See issue https://github.com/PyPSA/pypsa-usa/issues/487
Ratio of pipeline route length to the great circle distance between the centers of the two states. The length scales the compressor fuel and leakage losses of the pipeline.

If false, the capacities of gas production, underground storage (store, injection and withdrawal) and pipelines between states are fixed. If true, they are optimised between zero and the existing capacity, so assets whose fixed O&M outweighs their value can shrink. The injection of each storage keeps at least the share of its existing capacity that its store and withdrawal keep. Trade pipelines and linepack stay fixed.
How underground storage reservoirs are aggregated. ``state`` builds one storage per state; ``formation`` builds one per state and formation (depleted field, aquifer, salt dome).
Assumptions for the gas held in the pipelines (linepack), given for the ``interstate`` and ``intrastate`` pipeline classes of the EIA pipeline layer.
Count the pipelines of this class towards the linepack.
Inner diameter assumed for every pipeline of this class.
Maximum operating pressure. Sets the capacity of the linepack store.
Minimum operating pressure. Sets the lowest level the linepack store may reach.
Options of methane emission accounting attached to natural gas networks
Upstream per_unit leakage rate of natural gas. Applied to gas processing facilities.
Downstream per_unit leakage rate of natural gas. Applied to all end-use technologies that use natural gas.
Global warming potential of methane. GWP of 1 represents same carbon intensity as burned natural gas.
